proposals.before: In 1354 the court appointed Yu Hanlin attendant compiler and Gentleman for Discussion, sent envoys bearing imperial wine and famous silks, and summoned him by sea.
proposals.after: In 1354 the court appointed Yu as Hanlin attendant compiler and Gentleman for Discussion, sent envoys bearing imperial wine and famous silks, and summoned him by sea.
proposals.reason: English fuses 'Yu' with 'Hanlin', obscuring that Yu is the person appointed to the Hanlin post.

proposals.before: In 1357, when Ming forces entered Huizhou, the defending commander was about to hand him over. Yu said, "Would I serve two dynasties!"
proposals.after: In 1357, when Ming forces entered Huizhou, the defending commander was about to bring him over. Yu said, "Would I serve two dynasties!"
proposals.reason: 致之 here means bringing/recruiting him to the Ming side, not merely handing him over as a prisoner.

decisions.reason: s0075 朝廷除玉翰林待制、奉議大夫 appoints 玉 to the offices 翰林待制 and 奉議大夫; without "as," "Yu Hanlin" can be misread as a fused personal name, so the proposed wording correctly separates the person from the Hanlin title.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 朝廷除玉翰林待制、奉議大夫

decisions.reason: s0080 守將將要致之, followed by 吾豈事二姓者耶, means the commander sought to bring Yu over into Ming service, not hand him over as a captive; "bring him over" matches 致之 and the refusal to serve two dynasties, and s0081 因被拘囚 follows that refusal.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 守將將要致之，玉曰：「吾豈事二姓者耶！」
